sentences.text: Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.16535 of 2024, an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant-Krishna Pal Singh.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.500/- and also under Section 506(2) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 2 years and with fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that incident is said to have occurred on 18.03.2022 at about 9:00 to 9:30 during the day and report has been lodged on 18.03.2022 at about 18:18 hours.
Distance of Police station from scene of incident is about 8 kilometers.
Thus, there is delay in lodging the FIR, which has not been explained by prosecution.
Further, name of appellant has been mentioned in FIR which is also an afterthought.

Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to deposition of prosecutrix and her father as well as other oral testimonies submits that in the instant case, identity of appellant is not established.

Prosecutrix did not depose that at the time of incident,
appellant informed her about his name.

It is also urged that if identity of appellant was not disputed,
then, 2 CRA-7787-2024 why TIP was conducted. It is also urged that before conducting TIP,
prosecutrix had already seen appellant, therefore, TIP is vitiated.
It is also urged that incident occurred on 18.03.2022 whereas TIP has been conducted on 12.05.2022.
Above delay also casts shadow of doubt over TIP.
After referring to deposition of doctor Richa Gupta, it is urged that no definite opinion with respect to rape has been by given by the Doctor.

Further, no external injury has been found on the person of the prosecutrix whereas looking to the place of incident, prosecutrix Krishna Pal Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50781175/
1 should have sustained external injuries on back side of her body.

sentences.text: So far as internal injuries are concerned, the same stands explained from para 10 of doctor Richa Gupta.
Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that prosecutrix's under garments has been sealed by doctor on 18.03.2022 but they have been seized on 20.03.2022.
There is nothing on record to show as to where above clothes were kept in between 18.03.2022 to 20.03.2022.
Further, in seizure memo, color of undergarments of prosecutrix is not mentioned.
In view of above, possibility of tempering cannot be ruled out.
It is also urged that if appellant had removed the prosecutrix's clothes before committing the offence, then, there can be no semen on undergarments of prosecutrix .
It is also urged that FSL draft is dated 25.03.2022 whereas articles for FSL/DNA have been sent on 03.04.2022.
Blood sample of appellant was taken on 17.11.2022.
DNA report is dated 31.01.2024.

After referring and relying upon Judgments in the cases of Rahul Vs. State of Delhi Ministry of Home Affairs and Another (2023) 1 SCC 83, Suresh Devidas Malche Vs. The State of Maharashtra decided on 15.03.2023 and Manoj, Others Vs. State of M.P. (2023) 2 SCC 353 and Kishan Lal @
Champa Yadav Vs. State of Chhattisgarh passed in CRA No.565/2022 decided on 22.02.2023, it is also urged that prosecution did not adduce any evidence with respect to the procedure adopted for conducting DNA.

sentences.text: Hence, DNA report is of no value.
Further, PW-6, 3 CRA-7787-2024 PW-7 and PW-9 have turned hostile.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
Thus, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant be suspended.
The prayer is opposed by learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State.
Perusal of submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant reveals that he has extensively referred and discussed evidence on record on merits.
This Court has examined evidence available on record in the light of submissions of learned counsel for the appellant as well as principle laid down i n
Rahul Vs. State of Delhi Ministry of Home Affairs (supra), Suresh Devidas Malche (supra), Manoj and others (supra)
and Kishan Lal @ Champa Yadav (Supra).

Having regard to nature and extent of evidence available on record, especially testimony of Dr.
Richa Gupta and MLC Ex.P/1 and deposition of prosecutrix, and written report etc., I deem it not proper to suspend jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, aforesaid I.A. is dismissed.
List for final hearing in due course.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE R Krishna Pal Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50781175/
